title: Zero-configuration, serverless SQL
description: SQLite needs no server, no setup, no administration: the database is a single ordinary file and the engine is a library linked into the application. Opening a database is opening a file. This is why SQLite ships inside phones, browsers, and airplanes.

demo.program:
import sqlite3
c=sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
print('sqlite version:',sqlite3.sqlite_version)
print('zero-config: the DB is a file')
demo.expected_output:
sqlite version: 3.45.1
zero-config: the DB is a file

title: Public domain license

title: ACID transactions
description: SQLite transactions are fully ACID even across crashes and power loss, using rollback journals or write-ahead logging. Reliability is not sacrificed for simplicity. Your data survives the crash.

title: Single-file portability

title: FTS5 full-text search
description: The FTS5 extension builds full-text indexes with BM25 ranking, tokenizers, and snippet highlighting — a real search engine inside the file. Small apps get search without a search server. FTS5 is criminally underused.

title: JSON1: JSON in SQL
description: The JSON1 extension stores, queries, and indexes JSON with -> and ->> operators and json_each table functions. Semi-structured data lives happily in relational tables. SQLite is a document store when you need one.

title: The RTREE spatial index
description: SQLite's built-in RTREE virtual table indexes bounding boxes for fast spatial lookups even without SpatiaLite. Proximity queries over rectangles need nothing else. RTREE is the lightweight geo option.

title: SpatiaLite: full GIS in the file
description: SpatiaLite adds OGC Simple Features SQL: geometry types, spatial indexes, and hundreds of functions (ST_Distance, ST_Within, ST_Buffer) loadable as an extension. A file-based PostGIS for local GIS work. Alessandro Furieri's extension made SQLite a GIS database.

demo.program: print("SELECT ST_Distance(a.geom,b.geom) FROM places a,places b;")
demo.expected_output: SELECT ST_Distance(a.geom,b.geom) FROM places a,places b;

title: Geometry columns and SRIDs

title: WAL mode for concurrency
description: Write-ahead logging lets readers proceed during writes, the standard tuning for apps with concurrent access. One PRAGMA changes the locking behavior. WAL is the modern default for multi-threaded apps.

title: Backup API and VACUUM
description: The online backup API copies a live database safely; VACUUM rebuilds the file to reclaim space and defragment. Maintenance is two commands. Small databases stay small with occasional vacuums.

title: Limits and when to graduate
description: SQLite handles gigabytes and high read concurrency beautifully; write-heavy multi-writer workloads and network access are the graduation signals toward client-server databases. Knowing the ceiling is part of using it well. Most apps never hit it.

demo.program: print('graduation signals: many writers, network access')
